claims.text: The API server (kube-apiserver) exposes the Kubernetes HTTP API; it is the front end of the control plane, and users, parts of the cluster and external components all communicate through it.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview > Components (kube-apiserver); The Kubernetes API

claims.text: kubectl is the command-line tool that communicates with a cluster's control plane using the Kubernetes API.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Reference > kubectl (Command line tool); Concepts > Overview > kubectl

claims.text: kubectl reads its kubeconfig from $HOME/.kube/config by default, or from the files listed in the KUBECONFIG environment variable; a kubeconfig holds clusters (server address), users (credentials) and contexts, plus current-context.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Configuration > Organizing Cluster Access Using kubeconfig Files

claims.text: kind create cluster --name donhang adds a context named kind-donhang (cluster and user kind-donhang) to the kubeconfig and sets it as current-context ('Set kubectl context to "kind-donhang"').
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Quick Start (Interacting With Your Cluster, kind-<name> context); outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/cluster-up.txt

claims.text: For a kind cluster the kubeconfig server is https://127.0.0.1:<port>, a host port kind maps to the control-plane container's API server port 6443; credentials are a client certificate and key (shown as DATA+OMITTED by kubectl config view).
claims.source_hint: executed: kubectl config view --minify; docker port donhang-control-plane (6443/tcp -> 127.0.0.1:51407)

claims.text: kubectl get nodes sends GET /api/v1/nodes (with ?limit=500) to the API server, which answers 200 OK with a list of Node objects; kubectl prints selected fields as a table.
claims.source_hint: executed: kubectl get nodes -v=6 (kubectl v1.34.3): Response verb=GET url=https://127.0.0.1:51407/api/v1/nodes?limit=500 status=200 OK; API reference Node list

claims.text: Node components report node status to the API server over HTTPS (the kubelet posts node status/heartbeats); the Ready status kubectl shows comes from that record.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Architecture > Nodes (Node status, heartbeats); Control plane-node communication

claims.text: kubectl config current-context reads only the kubeconfig and sends no request to the API server (kubectl config current-context -v=6 logs no Response line).
claims.source_hint: kubectl reference: kubectl config current-context; executed with -v=6

claims.text: scripts/k8s/get-nodes.sh@stage-2 lines 5-12 define show() (echo '$ cmd' then run it) and run kubectl config current-context, then kubectl get nodes; captured output prints kind-donhang and three nodes Ready, v1.34.11.
The ROLES column of kubectl get nodes is derived from node-role.kubernetes.io/<role> labels; in the kind cluster only the control-plane node has such a label, so workers show <none>.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Reference > Well-Known Labels (node-role.kubernetes.io/*); executed kubectl get nodes --show-labels

claims.text: The VERSION column shows the kubelet version each node reports (v1.34.11 for kindest/node:v1.34.11).

kubectl -v=6 logs each request (verb, URL, status) to stderr; with 2>&1 | grep nodes one line remains: GET .../api/v1/nodes?limit=500 200 OK (kubectl adds limit=500). With a cold discovery cache kubectl first also GETs /api and /apis.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Reference > kubectl > Kubectl output verbosity and debugging; executed kubectl v1.34.3

claims.text: kubectl works from any machine whose kubeconfig has a reachable API server address and valid credentials; it does not need to run on a node.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Accessing Clusters; Organizing Cluster Access Using kubeconfig Files

claims.text: When the API server is not reachable (cluster stopped), kubectl get nodes fails with a connection error even though the kubeconfig is unchanged.
claims.source_hint: kubectl behaviour; kubernetes.io Troubleshooting kubectl (connection refused)

claims.text: The API server checks the credentials (client certificate and key for kind) of each request; a request with credentials it does not accept gets an error status code instead of the data.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Controlling Access to the Kubernetes API (authentication step)

claims.text: kubectl config view --minify removes all information not used by the current context from the output; credentials are shown as DATA+OMITTED unless --raw is given.
